newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, June S&P lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, June S&P lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished a lackluster session mixed, with June Standard and Poor's 500 futures lower.
June posted a relatively tight session, dipping below Wednesday's low of 836.50, but staying mostly within that day's range.

A long holiday weekend looms, stifling pit activity today and probably again Friday, traders said. Stock index futures will hold regular trading hours Friday and be shut Monday for Memorial Day. Debt futures close early on Friday, and many said stocks could languish Friday afternoon.

June S&P 500s barely reacted to minutes from the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Those minutes revealed that the decision to raise rates in March was unanimous, and a few policy makers preferred a bigger increase.
The Fed group also voted unanimously to adopt a so-called symmetric directive that did not bias policy toward either tightening or loosening during the period leading up to the meeting on May 20.
Before the opening, initial weekly jobless claims rose to 322,000 in the May 17 week from a revised 317,000 in the prior week.
Overall, traders called the market directionless.
"I was shellshocked with boredom," one S&P 500 trader said.
A few traders said weakness in technology stocks after their recent rally weighed slightly on the market.

At the close, June S&Ps were off 2.65 at 840.25, KCBT Value Lines were up 2.50 at 744.45, NYSE Composites were down 0.70 at 437.10, Nikkeis were off 10 at 19,930, Midcap 400s were 0.10 higher at 273.00, Nadsaq 100s were 2.00 lower at 950.75 and Russell 2000s were up 2.15 at 374.45. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
